id: Manon - with Pene Pati and Amina Edris-St James Theatre, 77-87 Courtenay Place, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Manon - with Pene Pati and Amina Edris
venue: St James Theatre, 77-87 Courtenay Place, Wellington
long_description:
Wellington Opera proudly presents Manon, Jules Massenet’s quintessentially French opera of the belle époque.

Amina Edris enchants audiences worldwide with her radiant soprano voice and captivating stage presence, while Pene Pati is beloved by many for his role in the chart-topping trio Sol3 Mio, and has since become one of the most sought-after tenors on the global stage. Phillip Rhodes returns following his wonderful performances in La Traviata and Lucia di Lammermoor.

Wellington Opera brings these wonderful Kiwi artists home to perform this sumptuous masterpiece at the St James Theatre, Wellington with French conductor Romain Dumas and Aotearoa’s renowned opera director Sara Brodie.

For one week only!

long_description:
Playcentres across the Wellington region invite whānau with tamariki from birth to school age to come along for a free visit during Playcentre Open Week, which runs from 17-21 August.

Playcentre is a place for you and your tamariki to play, learn and grow together and make connections with other whānau in your community.

id: Glass Bead-Making Taster - Winter Special!-Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki-Event Finder
name: Glass Bead-Making Taster - Winter Special!
venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
long_description:
Join us for this fabulous introduction to working with colourful molten glass at the Winter Special Price!

This class is a great way for absolute beginners to get a taste of working with glass to produce beautiful beads that can be used in a myriad of ways, including making a unique gift for your loved one (or yourself!).

As one of the earliest forms of human adornment, beads have long functioned as a way to express individuality, and what better way to do that than to learn to make your own unique beads?

Students are shown correct lampworking techniques to produce several decorative beads in just 3 hours! How many beads you make is up to you; some students make up to 10 while others make fewer using trickier techniques.

Kids over 12 (or so) are welcome to take the class, but anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

id: Stained Glass Suncatcher Day-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Stained Glass Suncatcher Day
venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
long_description:
Create gorgeous simple leadlight suncatchers with Lisa Sinclair.

A super fun day-class, ideal as a stand-alone experience, or as a day to get stuck into projects with your tutor at hand.

Beginners choose from a range of achievable patterns and choose their colour palette. They will learn to cut the glass, and prepare it before foiling and soldering each piece, creating a simple elegant colourful glass project.

The aim of this one day class is to leave with a completed small leadlight glass item.

More experienced students may bring existing projects to work on in class - though emphasis will be placed on focusing on the same techniques of flat, nicely soldered simple designs.

This is a warm and friendly class with excellent support and learning for complete beginners and more advanced students. All tools are supplied, though you are welcome to bring your own tools and glass if you have them.

Your materials for your beginner project are supplied as part of your course fee.
Additional materials and tools are available to purchase.

Not suitable for children. Older teenagers (16+) are welcome.

long_description:
So you've made a knife or bought a beautiful knife? Now it's time to make a customised leather sheath to house your knife.
Come along to a one day workshop and join others in finishing a professionally made sheath. Tim will help you design a properly fitted sheath complete with a welt if needed. (You might need to look that up.)

All materials are included in the cost of the workshop , so you need pay no more. He will also assist you in design, decoration, hand sewing, construction, dyeing, and fitting. Classes number no more than 6 people so you will get Tim's full attention and help. Be sure to bring your knife.

To book, all you need do is go to www.theleathery.co.nz and click on courses. Click on Knife Sheath Workshop and make your booking. You can even pay on the website after making your booking.

id: Cooking Classes-Sheila's Indian Kitchen, Ashton Fitchett Dr, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Cooking Classes
venue: Sheila's Indian Kitchen, Ashton Fitchett Dr, Wellington
long_description:
Authentic Indian cooking classes in Wellington with panaromic views over Wellington Harbour.

In each class, you will learn 4-5 recipes like: potato stuff roti, roasted eggplant curry, wholemeal, roti, naan; shahi paneer; dhal, samosa; palak paneer; gourmet chickpeas; vegetable korma; gulab jamun; kheer; mango lassi; masala chai, and many more...

The classes start at 6 pm or 10:30 am on weekends and weekdays with a 2-hour session followed by a dinner or lunch afterwards. The ingredients, copies of recipes, organic karma drink will be provided with a full course meal in a banquet setting. Custom made classes available for gluten free, dairy free and any other food intolerance and dietary requirements.The ingredients, recipes, complimentary organic karma drinks will be provided with a full course meal.

There are 2 to 8 people in each class in purpose built cooking studio. Also a private cooking classes available.

The menu for the class can be:

1) Spicy potato stuffed paratha and roti, rajasthani tomato relish, aalu matter or spicy peas- potato curry, roasted cumin yogurt raita and fresh mint- coriander chutney.

2) Shahi Paneer (cottage cheese cubes with spices and rich tomato-cashew gravy), garlic coriander naan, cumin jeera basmati rice and sweet fragrant rice pudding with cardamom. Also I will teach how to make fresh paneer.

3) Roasted eggplant curry, plain whole wheat chapatti or roti, jeera aaloo or potato curry, Tuar dahl (split yellow lentil) and Basmati rice with homemade pickle.

4) Palak paneer (creamy spinach curry with cubes of paneer), jeera rice (basmati rice with fragrant spices, panjabi chhole or spicy chickpeas curry and mango lassi. Also fresh paneer making.

5) Khadi (chickpeas fritters in yogurt and chickpeas flour soupy gravy), Aloo-Gobhi (cauliflower and potato curry),  savoury wraps with herbs and spices, fresh pickle and basmati rice.

The total cost is $130 per person, this includes ingredient cost. (As an alternative we also sell cooking class gift vouchers.The food options are unlimited and the class provides fresh and best ingredients)
For booking a class please contact indiancooking@xtra.co.nz

Just bring your taste buds! and Enjoy!!

long_description:
A hands-on, one-day workshop blending mindfulness, neuroscience, and self-awareness to help you feel better, relate better, and live with more clarity and purpose. (NZ Citizens and residents free with photo ID, all others pay $149).

Mindful Awareness – One-Day Workshop

Course is free for NZ citizens and residents (please bring photo ID when attending workshop). If you are not a NZ citizen or resident a fee of $149 will apply, please phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.

“If we don’t know what we’re doing, how can we do what we want?”

A hands-on, one-day workshop blending mindfulness, neuroscience, and self-awareness to help you feel better, relate better, and live with more clarity and purpose.

What you’ll get:

Simple tools to soothe stress and calm your system
Strategies to respond wisely instead of reacting on autopilot
Insight into your feelings, needs and inner patterns
Cutting-edge knowledge of the Vagus nerve and how it shapes your wellbeing
An intro to Parts Work: understand the different parts of you and how they work together
Practical ways to build creativity, clarity and genuine connection
Skills to feel stronger in yourself, your relationships and your work life
Everyday tools for better health, resilience and emotional balance
Real tools. Real change. Backed by science, grounded in practice.

Tea and coffee provided, please bring your lunch and snacks, and pen and paper to take notes.

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

id: Passkey to the Inner Worlds-Ōtaki Memorial Hall, Main St, Ōtaki-Event Finder
name: Passkey to the Inner Worlds
venue: Ōtaki Memorial Hall, Main St, Ōtaki
long_description:
Open your heart and your spiritual eye with the HU mantra.

HU is a sacred sound and ancient mantra. It is a love song to God that can uplift people of any religion, culture, or walk of life. When sung or chanted with an open heart, it opens the lines of communication to the most sacred part of yourself.

Singing HU acts as a tuning fork, aligning Soul to higher states of love, creativity, healing, and awareness.

You are welcome to join others in chanting this ancient mantra for fifteen to twenty minutes, followed by a short time for contemplation. Afterwards, enjoy spiritual conversation with others of like heart.

Receive a free beautifully illustrated Raise Your Spiritual IQ Experience Journal with simple, yet powerful tools to find the spiritual treasure within you.

Venue: Otaki Memorial Hall supper room, 9 Aotaki Street

Feel free to register or just drop in. We would love to see you!

For more information please contact Dave Phone: 021 214 1668

Presented by Eckankar, a worldwide spiritual teaching that offers tools and techniques for each individual to discover truth for themselves, through direct personal experience.

id: Thriving Through Change: Growing Resilience & Cultivating Courage-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Thriving Through Change: Growing Resilience & Cultivating Courage
venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
long_description:
Transform uncertainty into your greatest strength with a one-day journey of mindfulness, creativity, and self-discovery. Step out of survival mode and build a practical roadmap to live and work with unshakeable courage. (NZ citizen and residents free with ID, all others pay $120).

Thriving Through Change: Growing Resilience & Cultivating Courage

This course is free for NZ citizens and residents. Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.

If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.

Cultivating true resilience is an intentional practice of the mind, body, and soul. It is rooted in deep self-knowledge and personal empowerment. In our rapidly changing world, the ultimate question we must ask ourselves is: How can I unlock my unique strengths and capacities to not just survive these demanding times, but truly thrive?

By implementing a "living" practice of mindful strategies, creative expression, and physical awareness, we can empower our thinking, elevate our emotional well-being, and bring a renewed vitality to our life's work.

What to Expect

This workshop offers you a rich tapestry of practical tools, storytelling, and collaborative discussion. Together, we will explore diverse pathways to foster courage, helping you shift from a state of survival to one of thriving—even while navigating the daily pressures of stress, grief, anxiety, or the fear of an uncertain future.

What You Will Take Away:

Mindful Strategies: Daily, actionable practices to anchor your thoughts and reduce overwhelm.
Creative & Physical Outlets: Expressive tools to release tension and process complex emotions.
A Personal Roadmap: A clearer understanding of your innate strengths to help you navigate future transitions with confidence.
Details & What to Bring:

Duration: Full-day workshop
What to bring: A personal journal and your favourite pen or pencil. (However, paper and pen will be provided if you need).
Step out of the survival loop. Join us to reclaim your inner strength and cultivate the courage to thrive.

NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your session.

Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

id: Pub Sing-Boundary Tap & Kitchen, 3 Raumati Rd, Raumati-Event Finder
name: Pub Sing
venue: Boundary Tap & Kitchen, 3 Raumati Rd, Raumati
long_description:
Pub Sing - where the audience turns into the choir at the pub, with a live rock band,

No sheet music, no experience needed, and absolutely no solos.

Katy reveals three songs on the night (usually a crowd-pleaser, a ballad, and a banger), and even if you don’t know them, you’ll pick them up fast with colour-coded lyrics on screen.

You learn different harmony options, sing along with the band, and blend into a room of up to 80 voices, so no one’s listening to you; they’re singing with you.

There’s banter, laughs, a bit of silliness, and a whole lot of feel-good energy. It’s not karaoke (shudder), it’s everyone singing together just for the fun of it, and it’s the perfect end-of-week lift you needed.

*Please check the ticket booking link for updates or changes to dates*
*All ticket sales goes directly to the band*
